_readme: Declarative shot list for tools/capture/capture.mjs. See tools/capture/README.md.
Per-shot fields:
id           required, unique, filename-safe. Output is <out>/<id>.png.
description  one line, shown in logs, report.json and contact-sheet labels.
url          page path, resolved against the server origin. Query params are
kept; the harness always forces ?autostart=0 and ?backend=<backend>.
backend      'webgl2' (default) or 'webgpu'.
setup        JS run after the engine is ready, BEFORE the warmup frames.
warmupFrames deterministic frames stepped at a fixed 1/60 s delta, so temporal
effects converge and animation reaches a known pose.
pose         JS run AFTER the warmup, immediately before the capture render.
Use for the camera: modules re-drive the camera every update, so a
camera set in `setup` is overwritten during the warmup.
mode         'readback' (default, GPU->RenderTarget->PNG, no DOM) or
'screenshot' (page.screenshot, includes DOM/HUD layers).
guard        per-shot blank-frame threshold overrides.
Scripts are strings, or arrays of lines joined with newlines. They run as async
function bodies with these bindings: d2rim, engine, ctx, scene, camera, renderer,
time, services, events, THREE.
`d2rim.render` is the assembled frame graph (settings, post, timeOfDay, sky,
lighting, gtao, ibl, ssr, materials, volumetrics, lightShafts) and `d2rim.scene`
is the BloodMoor module. `d2rim.scene.field.heightAt(x, z)` is the same terrain
height function the scene places props with, so a pose can put the camera a known
distance above the ground instead of guessing at it.
Scene facts these shots are composed against (src/scene/BloodMoor.ts):
campfire at (3.1, ground, -5.2) - the focal point, and the only warm light
Barbarian at (1.1, ground, 0.4), facing the fire
ruined masonry wall centred near (-5.6, -11.4), running at 24 deg
rock escarpment along x ~ -13, dead-tree ridge line peaking near z ~ -36
three oversized framing dead trees at (-7.6, 5.4), (13.4, 2.4) and (9.4, -14.6)
a worn mud track written into the ground material, (14.6, 17.5) -> the fire
broken fence runs (13.5, 15.5) -> (8.9, -12.8): the leading line
time of day: bloodMoor preset at 12.15 h, lat 51, day 305, full overcast
exposure is LOCKED (autoExposure off, exposure 1.35). Every shot, every
backend and every quality tier must therefore share one tonal response -
if two shots of this scene disagree on brightness, that is a bug, not a
framing difference.

shots.description: Wide establishing: the whole Blood Moor composition - foreground rubble, campfire and Barbarian in the midground, treed ridge behind, aerial perspective separating all three.
pose: // The authored camera. The basin, the fence line and the wall angle were
// all composed for exactly this eye position, so this is the frame the

shots.description: Fog and god rays: low across the basin along the sun bearing, so the froxel fog pooling in the hollow sits between the lens and the shafts breaking through the ridge treeline.
pose: // Shafts are a forward-scattering effect: they only exist within about
// 35 deg of the sun vector. The bearing is therefore read from the live
// sun rather than hard-coded, so this frame stays correct if the time of
const eye = new THREE.Vector3(target.x - bearing.x * 15.5, 0, target.z - bearing.y * 15.5);

shots.description: Warm/cold contrast: close on the campfire with the Barbarian rimmed by it and cold overcast key on everything outside its falloff. The most diagnostic frame in the set for colour separation.
pose: // Three-quarters onto the fire from 5 m, so the firelit side and the
// sky-lit side of both the figure and the ground are in frame at once. If
// the grade has crushed the image to grey mush it fails here first.

shots.description: Material close-up: parallax-mapped wet masonry filling the left of frame against wet mud and dead grass, at the raking angle where parallax occlusion actually shows.
pose: // A few metres off the wall and about 20 deg from its surface normal.
// Head-on, parallax occlusion mapping is nearly indistinguishable from a
// normal map; at a raking angle the stones occlude each other and the
// courses gain real depth. Low enough that the mud/grass blend line runs
// through the bottom third, so both materials read at 1:1.
// The eye height must be measured at the *eye*, not at the subject.
// Reading the wall's ground height and adding to it put the camera
// inside the bank when the ground rose between the two, which is why
// this shot was photographing the inside of a hill.

shots.description: Shadow and contact detail: raking view across the campsite clutter, for CSM softness, cascade transitions, peter-panning and GTAO contact darkening.
pose: // Down the shadow bearing from 3.6 m onto the clutter cluster, where
// there are enough small objects resting on the ground that contact
// occlusion and shadow bias errors have nowhere to hide.

shots.description: Backlit silhouette: camera into the sun with the Barbarian and the ridge trees between, for rim separation, highlight rolloff and how the tone curve handles the brightest thing in the scene.
pose: // On the sun bearing, past the figure, at eye height. This is where an
// over-eager bloom or a tone curve with no shoulder announces itself: the
// sun is behind a full overcast slab, so what should reach the lens is a
// broad soft glow - never a disc, and never a flare.

shots.description: Third-person framing: the Barbarian over-the-shoulder at the distance the game will play at, idle animation settled. Proof the 41-joint rig loads, binds and animates.
pose: // The gameplay camera: 4.2 m back, 1.85 m up, 0.55 m off the spine axis,
// aimed at chest height. Deliberately the real third-person rig rather
// than a flattering portrait lens - if the character reads badly from
// here it reads badly in the game.
const base = hero ? hero.position.clone() : new THREE.Vector3(1.1, 0, 0.4);

shots.description: Distant terrain and aerial perspective: elevated view down the length of the moor. The subject is the gradient, not any object.
pose: // From the top of the west bank, looking north-east down the moor. Near
// ground should keep its own colour, the ridge should sit distinctly in
// front of the sky, and the transition should be smooth. Banding, a flat
// grey wash, or a ridge that vanishes into the sky are all failures.

shots.description: ?quality=low: FXAA, no GTAO, no SSR, two 1024 cascades, 0.75 render scale. Same framing as wide-establishing so the tier ladder compares side by side.
?quality=ultra: TAA 16 plus sharpen, full-resolution GTAO, high SSR, four 3072 cascades. The other end of the ladder from quality-low.
HUD composite (page.screenshot): the DOM overlay layered over the rendered frame, for UI legibility against a dark, low-contrast image.
WebGPU backend parity: byte-for-byte the same pose, resolution and warmup as wide-establishing, on the other backend. This IS a tonal comparison - the two frames must agree.
pose: // Identical to wide-establishing in every respect except the backend.
// This shot asked for 20 warmup frames and for a long time never got
// them: the harness silently clamped WebGPU warmup to 0, because
// presenting the swapchain in this container loses the device. So it
// photographed frame 0 against a 20-frame WebGL2 reference and the
// parity gate dutifully reported the resulting 0.12 of mean luminance
// as a *backend* divergence. It was not: with no warmup TAA has no
// the froxel volume has not converged and the scene module's update()
// has never run, so the fire never flickers into existence. Comparing an
// unconverged frame against a converged one measures the harness, not
// the renderer. Captured cold at the same warmup the two backends agree
// to 0.0004 of mean luminance. The warmup now renders into the capture
// target rather than the swapchain, on both backends, via
// PostStack.setHeadlessPresentation - so the two sides really do
// converge identically and any difference left here is a real bug and
// is meant to be read as one.
